records.literal_gloss: And sent Hiram king of Tyre messengers to David, and trees of cedars, and craftsmen of wall and craftsmen of wood, to build for him a house.

en.L: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and craftsmen of wall and craftsmen of wood, to build a house for him.
en.B: Hiram king of Tyre sent envoys to David, with cedar logs, stonemasons and woodworkers, to build him a palace.
en.R: Hiram, the king of Tyre, sent messengers to David. He also sent cedar logs and workers skilled with stone and wood, to build a palace for David.

es.L: Y Hiram rey de Tiro envió mensajeros a David, y troncos de cedro, y artesanos de muro y artesanos de madera, para edificarle una casa.
es.B: Hiram, rey de Tiro, envió embajadores a David, con troncos de cedro, canteros y carpinteros, para construirle un palacio.
es.R: Hiram, el rey de Tiro, envió mensajeros a David. También le mandó troncos de cedro y trabajadores expertos en piedra y en madera, para construirle un palacio a David.

fr.L: Et Hiram, roi de Tyr, envoya à David des messagers, et des bois de cèdre, et des artisans de la pierre de mur et des artisans du bois, pour lui bâtir une maison.
fr.B: Hiram, roi de Tyr, envoya des messagers à David, avec du bois de cèdre, des tailleurs de pierre et des charpentiers, pour lui bâtir un palais.
fr.R: Hiram, le roi de Tyr, a envoyé des messagers à David. Il a aussi envoyé du bois de cèdre et des ouvriers habiles à travailler la pierre et le bois, pour construire un palais pour David.

sw.L: Hiramu mfalme wa Tiro akatuma wajumbe kwa Daudi, na miti ya mierezi, na mafundi wa ukuta na mafundi wa mbao, ili wamjengee nyumba.
sw.B: Hiramu mfalme wa Tiro alituma wajumbe kwa Daudi, pamoja na magogo ya mierezi, mafundi wa mawe na mafundi seremala, ili wamjengee jumba la kifalme.
sw.R: Hiramu, mfalme wa Tiro, alituma wajumbe kwa Daudi. Alituma pia magogo ya mierezi na mafundi stadi wa mawe na wa mbao, ili wamjengee Daudi jumba la kifalme.

vi.R: Hi-ram, vua thành Ty-rơ, sai sứ giả đến gặp Đa-vít. Vua cũng gửi gỗ bá hương cùng những người thợ giỏi nghề đá và nghề mộc đến để xây cho Đa-vít một cung điện.

decisions.choice: Hiram king of Tyre: ruler of a rich trading city on the coast north of Israel
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:11: Tyre was a Phoenician port, famous for its trade and its builders, and cedar from the mountains of Lebanon behind it was the finest building timber of the region. The same king later supplied Solomon with cedar and workers for the temple (1 Kings 5:15-25).

decisions.choice: Hiram
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters spell the name Huram, the form 2 Chronicles uses for this king (2 Chronicles 2:2). The form marked to be read aloud is Hiram, as in 2 Samuel 5:11 and Kings, and it is followed here. Both are spellings of one name.

decisions.choice: a house: a palace
decisions.reason: The word "house" is used for any dwelling. Built of cedar by skilled workers, this is David's palace, the "house of cedars" he speaks of in 17:1.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 14:1-2 retells 2 Samuel 5:11-12, with small differences
decisions.reason: Chronicles says Hiram sent the men "to build him a house", where 2 Samuel 5:11 says "and they built a house for David": the purpose, not yet the result. It names the craftsmen of the wall before those of wood, the reverse of 2 Samuel, and says "craftsmen of wall" without the word "stone".

decisions.choice: stonemasons and woodworkers (Balanced); workers skilled with stone and wood (Readable); palace
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:11, Balanced and Readable use the ordinary words for these trades, and call the king's house a palace. "Craftsmen of wall" are those who build walls of cut stone.

decisions.choice: "석수들과 목수들을 보내어 ... 짓게 했다"
decisions.reason: The Korean of 2 Samuel 5:11 is kept, with the two changes of Chronicles: the stone workers come before the wood workers, and the building is the purpose of the sending ("짓게 했다"), not yet its result.

records.literal_gloss: And knew David that had established him Yahweh as king over Israel, that was exalted to above his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.

en.L: And David knew that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had established him as king over Israel, that his kingdom was highly exalted for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.
en.B: Then David knew that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made him secure as king over Israel, and had raised his kingdom very high for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.
en.R: Then David understood that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made him king over Israel and made his kingdom very great. He did it for the good of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.

es.L: Y supo David que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había establecido como rey sobre Israel, que su reino había sido muy enaltecido por amor a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo Israel.
es.B: Entonces David supo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había afirmado como rey sobre Israel, y que había engrandecido mucho su reino por amor a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo Israel.
es.R: Entonces David comprendió que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había hecho rey de Israel y había engrandecido mucho su reino. Lo hizo por el bien de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo Israel.

fr.L: Et David sut que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait affermi comme roi sur Israël, et que son royaume était élevé très haut à cause de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple Israël.
fr.B: David reconnut alors que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait établi solidement comme roi sur Israël, et que son royaume avait été élevé très haut à cause de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple Israël.
fr.R: Alors David a compris que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait fait roi sur Israël et qu’il avait rendu son royaume très puissant. Il avait fait cela pour le bien de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple Israël.

sw.L: Daudi akajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemthibitisha kuwa mfalme juu ya Israeli, kwamba ufalme wake umeinuliwa juu sana kwa ajili ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Israeli.
sw.B: Ndipo Daudi akajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemwimarisha kuwa mfalme juu ya Israeli, na ameuinua juu sana ufalme wake kwa ajili ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Israeli.
sw.R: Ndipo Daudi akaelewa kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemfanya mfalme juu ya Israeli na kuufanya ufalme wake kuwa mkuu sana. Alifanya hivyo kwa faida ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Israeli.

vi.L: Đa-vít biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập vững ông làm vua trên Y-sơ-ra-ên, rằng vương quốc ông đã được tôn lên rất cao vì cớ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đa-vít biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập vững ngôi vua của ông trên Y-sơ-ra-ên, và đã tôn vương quốc ông lên rất cao vì cớ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Bấy giờ Đa-vít hiểu rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập ông làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên và làm cho vương quốc ông rất lớn mạnh. Ngài làm vậy vì lợi ích của dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.B: 그때 다윗은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 자기를 이스라엘의 왕으로 든든히 세우시고, 그분의 백성 이스라엘을 위하여 자기 나라를 매우 높이셨다는 것을 알았다.
ko.R: 그때 다윗은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 자기를 이스라엘의 왕으로 세우시고 자기 나라를 아주 강하게 해 주셨다는 것을 깨달았다. 그분께서는 그분의 백성 이스라엘을 위해 그렇게 하셨다.

decisions.choice: had established him: had set him firmly in place as king
decisions.reason: The verb means to make firm or secure, as at 2 Samuel 5:12. It is the word Yahweh uses in his promise that he will establish the kingdom of David's son (17:11-12).

decisions.choice: for the sake of his people Israel: Yahweh's people
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:12, "his people" is best taken as Yahweh's people ("my people Israel", 11:2). David has been made great for the good of the nation that belongs to God.

decisions.choice: highly exalted: stronger than 2 Samuel 5:12
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:12 says only that David's kingdom "was lifted up". Chronicles adds a word meaning "upward" or "to the height", so that the kingdom was raised very high. It also lacks the "and" before the second "that", so the exalting of the kingdom reads as part of what it meant for Yahweh to establish David. The verb is passive, but Yahweh is the one who lifts the kingdom up.

decisions.choice: had raised his kingdom very high (Balanced); made his kingdom very great. He did it for the good of (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:12, Balanced and Readable turn the passive verb into an active one with Yahweh as subject, and add "very" for the word "upward". Readable splits the sentence in two.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 14:3 differs from 2 Samuel 5:13
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:13 says David took "concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David". Chronicles names wives only, says "in Jerusalem", leaves out the move from Hebron (told at 11:1-9), and makes David the subject: "David fathered more sons and daughters".

decisions.choice: more: added to the sons born at Hebron
decisions.reason: The word "more" looks back to David's household at Hebron, whose six sons are listed at 3:1-4.

decisions.choice: more wives: a sign of a king's power
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:13, many wives were a sign of a king's power and wealth, and some marriages sealed alliances. The law warned a king not to take many wives (Deuteronomy 17:17).

decisions.choice: became the father of (Balanced); married ... had (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in the genealogies ("begot"); Balanced uses the same wording as the lists in chapters 1-9, and Readable says "had". Readable says "married" for "took" wives.

decisions.choice: akaoa wake zaidi
decisions.reason: Chronicles names only wives, where 2 Samuel 5:13 adds concubines; "kuoa" says plainly that David married them.

decisions.choice: the list of 2 Samuel 5:14-16 and 1 Chronicles 3:5-8
decisions.reason: Verses 4-7 give the sons born in Jerusalem again. Like 1 Chronicles 3:5-8 the list has thirteen names, where 2 Samuel 5:14-16 has eleven: it adds Elpelet (verse 5) and Nogah (verse 6), and has Beeliada for Eliada (verse 7). This verse spells the first name Shammua, as 2 Samuel does, where 1 Chronicles 3:5 has Shimea, and adds the words "who were his".

decisions.choice: Nathan and Solomon: sons through whom David's line continued
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:14: Solomon succeeded David as king, and Nathan is named in the line of Jesus in Luke 3:31. 1 Chronicles 3:5 says the first four were the sons of Bathshua (Bathsheba).

decisions.choice: the children (Balanced); the sons (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:14. The Hebrew says "those born"; every name in the list is a son's, so Readable says "sons".

decisions.choice: the list of verses 4-7 is one Korean sentence closed by "-이다" in verse 7
decisions.reason: As 2 Samuel 5:14-16 in Korean; the names stay under their own verse numbers.

decisions.reason: Nogah is named here and at 1 Chronicles 3:7, but not in 2 Samuel 5:15, which goes straight from Elishua to Nepheg. Nothing more is told of him, or of Nepheg and Japhia.

decisions.reason: As noted at 2 Samuel 5:16, the names mean "the Lord knows" (Beeliada) and "God knows" (Eliada). Beeliada uses the word baal in its plain sense "lord" or "master"; the other lists have the form with El, "God", in its place.

decisions.choice: thirteen sons, with no total given
decisions.reason: The list ends without a count, unlike 1 Chronicles 3:8 ("nine", after the four of 3:5). Two pairs of names are alike (Elishua and Elishama, Elpelet and Eliphelet); as at 3:8, David may have had two sons of a similar name, or a name may have been repeated in copying.

records.literal_gloss: And heard Philistines that had been anointed David as king over all Israel, and went up all Philistines to seek David; and heard David and went out before them.

en.L: And [the] Philistines heard that David had been anointed [as] king over all Israel, and all the Philistines went up to seek David; and David heard [of it] and went out before them.
en.B: News reached the Philistines that David had been anointed king over all Israel, so the whole Philistine force went up to hunt for him. But David heard of it and went out to face them.
en.R: The Philistines heard that David had been made king over all Israel. So their whole army came up to search for him. But David heard about it and went out to fight them.

es.L: Y oyeron los filisteos que David había sido ungido [como] rey sobre todo Israel, y subieron todos los filisteos a buscar a David; y David [lo] oyó y salió delante de ellos.
es.B: Llegó a oídos de los filisteos que David había sido ungido rey sobre todo Israel, así que todas las fuerzas filisteas subieron a buscarlo. Pero David se enteró y salió a hacerles frente.
es.R: Los filisteos oyeron que David había sido hecho rey de todo Israel. Así que todo su ejército subió a buscarlo. Pero David se enteró y salió a pelear contra ellos.

fr.L: Et les Philistins apprirent que David avait été oint [comme] roi sur tout Israël, et tous les Philistins montèrent pour chercher David ; et David [l’]apprit et sortit au-devant d’eux.
fr.B: Les Philistins apprirent que David avait été oint comme roi sur tout Israël, et toutes leurs forces montèrent pour le traquer. Mais David l’apprit et sortit à leur rencontre.
fr.R: Les Philistins ont appris qu’on avait fait de David le roi de tout Israël. Alors toute leur armée est montée pour le chercher. Mais David l’a appris et il est sorti pour les combattre.

sw.L: Wafilisti wakasikia kwamba Daudi amepakwa mafuta [awe] mfalme juu ya Israeli wote, na Wafilisti wote wakapanda kumtafuta Daudi; naye Daudi akasikia [habari], akatoka kwenda kukutana nao.
sw.B: Habari zilipowafikia Wafilisti kwamba Daudi amepakwa mafuta kuwa mfalme juu ya Israeli wote, jeshi lote la Wafilisti likapanda kumsaka. Lakini Daudi akasikia habari hiyo, akatoka kwenda kukabiliana nao.
sw.R: Wafilisti walisikia kwamba Daudi amefanywa mfalme juu ya Israeli wote. Basi jeshi lao lote likapanda kumtafuta. Lakini Daudi alisikia habari hiyo, akatoka kwenda kupigana nao.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin nghe rằng Đa-vít đã được xức dầu làm vua trên cả Y-sơ-ra-ên, thì toàn thể người Phi-li-tin kéo lên để tìm Đa-vít; Đa-vít nghe [vậy] liền ra đối đầu với chúng.
vi.B: Khi người Phi-li-tin nghe tin Đa-vít đã được xức dầu làm vua trên cả Y-sơ-ra-ên, toàn quân Phi-li-tin kéo lên truy tìm ông. Nhưng Đa-vít nghe biết và ra đối đầu với họ.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin nghe tin Đa-vít đã được lập làm vua trên cả Y-sơ-ra-ên. Vì vậy toàn quân của họ kéo lên để lùng bắt ông. Nhưng Đa-vít biết được và ra đánh họ.

ko.L: 그리고 블레셋 사람들은 다윗이 기름 부음을 받아 온 이스라엘의 왕이 되었다는 것을 들었다. 그리고 모든 블레셋 사람이 다윗을 찾으려고 올라왔다. 그리고 다윗이 [그것을] 듣고 그들 앞으로 나갔다.
ko.B: 블레셋 사람들은 다윗이 기름 부음을 받아 온 이스라엘의 왕이 되었다는 소식을 듣고, 모든 군대가 다윗을 잡으려고 올라왔다. 그러나 다윗은 그 소식을 듣고 그들을 맞서러 나갔다.
ko.R: 블레셋 사람들은 다윗이 온 이스라엘의 왕이 되었다는 소식을 들었다. 그래서 그들의 온 군대가 다윗을 찾으러 올라왔다. 그러나 다윗은 그 소식을 듣고 그들과 싸우러 나갔다.

decisions.choice: the Philistines heard: a united Israel under David was now a threat to them
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:17: the Philistines had held power over much of Israel since Saul's defeat (10:1-7), and a king over all Israel was a danger they could not ignore.

decisions.choice: to seek David: to hunt him down
decisions.reason: To "seek" a person is often to look for him in order to kill him. The whole Philistine army sets out against him.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 14:8-17 retells 2 Samuel 5:17-25; differences in this verse
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:17 says "they had anointed David king over Israel"; Chronicles uses the passive and says "over all Israel", as it does at 11:1-3. Where 2 Samuel says David "went down to the stronghold", Chronicles says he "went out before them", that is, to meet them.

decisions.choice: went out before them: went out to face them in battle
decisions.reason: To "go out before" an enemy is to march out to meet him. Chronicles does not say where David first went; it shows him going out against the Philistines.

decisions.choice: the whole Philistine force (Balanced); their whole army (Readable); to face them / to fight them
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:17, "all the Philistines" means their full fighting force. Balanced and Readable say what going out "before them" means, as m4 explains.

decisions.choice: akatoka kwenda kukutana nao (L); kukabiliana nao (B); kupigana nao (R)
decisions.reason: Chronicles has David "go out before them" where 2 Samuel 5:17 has him go down to the stronghold; the Swahili follows Chronicles.

records.literal_gloss: And Philistines had come and made a raid in [the] valley of Rephaim.

en.L: And [the] Philistines had come and made a raid in the Valley of Rephaim.
en.B: Now the Philistines had come and made a raid on the Valley of Rephaim.
en.R: The Philistines came and raided the Valley of Rephaim.

es.L: Y los filisteos habían venido e hicieron una incursión en el valle de Refaim.
es.B: Los filisteos habían llegado y habían hecho una incursión en el valle de Refaim.
es.R: Los filisteos vinieron y saquearon el valle de Refaim.

fr.L: Et les Philistins étaient venus et avaient fait une incursion dans la vallée des Rephaïm.
fr.B: Or les Philistins étaient venus piller la vallée des Rephaïm.
fr.R: Les Philistins sont venus faire un raid dans la vallée des Rephaïm.

sw.L: Na Wafilisti walikuwa wamekuja wakavamia katika Bonde la Refaimu.
sw.B: Basi Wafilisti walikuwa wamekuja wakavamia Bonde la Refaimu.
sw.R: Wafilisti walikuja wakavamia Bonde la Refaimu.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin đã đến và cướp phá trong thung lũng Rê-pha-im.
vi.B: Bấy giờ người Phi-li-tin đã đến và cướp phá thung lũng Rê-pha-im.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin kéo đến và cướp phá thung lũng Rê-pha-im.

ko.L: 그리고 블레셋 사람들이 와서 르바임 골짜기를 습격했다.
ko.B: 그때 블레셋 사람들이 와서 르바임 골짜기를 습격했다.
ko.R: 블레셋 사람들은 와서 르바임 골짜기를 습격했다.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Rephaim: a broad valley just southwest of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:18: the valley lay on the border of Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:8) and was a natural route from the Philistine plain up into the hills.

decisions.choice: made a raid: in place of "spread out" in 2 Samuel 5:18
decisions.reason: Chronicles uses a different verb from 2 Samuel 5:18. It means to strip or plunder, and is used of raiders falling on a land (1 Samuel 23:27; 27:8). The two words describe the same thing: an army spread through the valley taking what it could.

decisions.choice: Bonde la Refaimu
decisions.reason: The valley is named as in 1 Chronicles 11:15; 2 Samuel 5:18 wrote "Bonde la Warefai", which a reviewer may prefer to settle on.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל דָּוִ֤יד בֵּאלֹהִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאֶֽעֱלֶה֙ עַל־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּנְתַתָּ֖ם בְּיָדִ֑י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֤וֹ יְהוָה֙ עֲלֵ֔ה וּנְתַתִּ֖ים בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And inquired David of God, saying, Shall I go up against Philistines, and will you give them into my hand? And said to him Yahweh, Go up, and I will give them into your hand.

en.L: And David inquired of God, saying, "Shall I go up against [the] Philistines, and will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give them into my hand?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Go up, and I will give them into your hand."
en.B: So David inquired of God, "Am I to go up against the Philistines? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hand them over to me?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered him, "Go up, and I will hand them over to you."
en.R: David asked God, "Should I go and attack the Philistines? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give me victory over them?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered him, "Go and attack them. I will give you victory over them."

es.L: Y consultó David a Dios, diciendo: «¿Subiré contra los filisteos? ¿Y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} los entregarás en mi mano?». Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «Sube, y yo los entregaré en tu mano».
es.B: Entonces David consultó a Dios: «¿Debo subir contra los filisteos? ¿Me los entregarás?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió: «Sube, y yo te los entregaré».
es.R: David le preguntó a Dios: «¿Debo ir a atacar a los filisteos? ¿Me darás la victoria sobre ellos?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió: «Ve y atácalos. Yo te daré la victoria sobre ellos».

fr.L: Et David consulta Dieu, en disant : « Monterai-je contre les Philistins ? Les livreras-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} entre mes mains ? » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui dit : « Monte, et je les livrerai entre tes mains. »
fr.B: David consulta donc Dieu : « Dois-je monter contre les Philistins ? Me les livreras-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui répondit : « Monte, et je te les livrerai. »
fr.R: David a demandé à Dieu : « Est-ce que je dois aller attaquer les Philistins ? Est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vas me donner la victoire sur eux ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a répondu : « Va les attaquer. Je vais te donner la victoire sur eux. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwuliza Mungu, akisema, "Je, nipande kupigana na Wafilisti? Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utawatia mkononi mwangu?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Panda, nami nitawatia mkononi mwako."
sw.B: Basi Daudi akamwuliza Mungu, "Je, nipande kupigana na Wafilisti? Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utawatia mikononi mwangu?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjibu, "Panda, nami nitawatia mikononi mwako."
sw.R: Daudi alimwuliza Mungu, "Je, niende kuwashambulia Wafilisti? Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utanipa ushindi juu yao?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjibu, "Nenda ukawashambulie. Nitakupa ushindi juu yao."

vi.L: Đa-vít cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời rằng: "Con có nên đi lên đánh người Phi-li-tin không? Ngài có trao chúng vào tay con không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với ông: "Hãy đi lên, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trao chúng vào tay ngươi."
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời: "Con có nên đi lên đánh người Phi-li-tin không? Ngài có trao chúng vào tay con không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Hãy đi lên, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trao chúng vào tay con."
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi Đức Chúa Trời: "Con có nên đi đánh người Phi-li-tin không? Ngài có cho con thắng họ không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Hãy đi đánh chúng. Ta sẽ cho con thắng chúng."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 하나님께 여쭈어 말했다. "제가 블레셋 사람들을 치러 올라가야 합니까? 그들을 제 손에 넘겨주시겠습니까?" 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "올라가거라. 내가 그들을 네 손에 넘겨주겠다."
ko.B: 그래서 다윗이 하나님께 여쭈었다. "제가 블레셋 사람들을 치러 올라가도 되겠습니까? 주님께서 그들을 제 손에 넘겨주시겠습니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "올라가거라. 내가 그들을 네 손에 넘겨주겠다."
ko.R: 다윗이 하나님께 여쭈었다. "제가 가서 블레셋 사람들을 칠까요? 주님께서 저에게 승리를 주시겠습니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "가서 그들을 쳐라. 내가 너에게 그들을 이기게 해 주겠다."

decisions.choice: inquired of God: asked God for an answer, probably through the priest
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:19, David seeks God's guidance before battle, likely through the priest and the ephod, which gave answers to questions like these (1 Samuel 23:2-4; 30:7-8).

decisions.choice: give into my hand: give me power over them, victory
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. To give an enemy into someone's hand is to grant victory over him.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 5:19
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:19 says David inquired "of Yahweh"; Chronicles has "of God" here and calls him God through the rest of the story (verses 11, 14-16), but keeps the name Yahweh for the one who answers. The answer is shorter: "and I will give them into your hand", without the doubled verb of 2 Samuel ("I will surely give") and without naming the Philistines. The two questions are joined by "and".

decisions.choice: asked; attack; give victory over
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:19, Readable says "asked" for "inquired of", "attack" for "go up against", and explains the idiom "give into the hand".

decisions.choice: ¿Y tú los entregarás? (L, with the span); ¿Me los entregarás? (B, R, no span)
decisions.reason: Literal writes the pronoun "tú" after "Y", so the deity_pronoun setting has a word to work on; Balanced and Readable leave the subject in the verb, as the Spanish of 2 Samuel 5:19 does, and so carry no span there.

decisions.choice: David prays in 합쇼체 with "제"; God answers in 해라체
decisions.reason: The Samuel note's speech levels, as in 2 Samuel 5:19; Chronicles has "inquired of God" where Samuel has "of the LORD", and the Korean follows.

decisions.choice: David prays with "con" and "Ngài"; God says "Ta" and calls David "ngươi" (L), "con" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The rule for God's words in Chronicles: God speaking to one person who serves him (David, Solomon, Elijah, a prophet) says "ngươi" at Literal and "con" at Balanced and Readable, as in Genesis and the Pentateuch; his words to a king he is judging, to Israel as a nation or to the nations stay "ngươi" / "các ngươi". David's prayer keeps the forms of 2 Samuel 5:19-24, which this passage retells; a pronoun for God that begins a sentence is written plainly with its capital, as the style guide says.

source.text: וַיַּעֲל֥וּ בְּבַֽעַל־פְּרָצִים֮ וַיַּכֵּ֣ם שָׁ֣ם דָּוִיד֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔יד פָּרַ֨ץ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֧ים אֶת־אוֹיְבַ֛י בְּיָדִ֖י כְּפֶ֣רֶץ מָ֑יִם עַל־כֵּ֗ן קָֽרְא֛וּ שֵֽׁם־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בַּ֥עַל פְּרָצִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went up to Baal-perazim, and struck them there David, and said David, Has broken through God my enemies by my hand like a breaking through of waters; therefore they called [the] name of the place that Baal-perazim.

en.L: And they went up to Baal-perazim, and David struck them there, and David said, "God has broken through my enemies by my hand like a breaking through of waters." Therefore they called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
en.B: So they went up to Baal-perazim, and David defeated them there. He said, "God has burst through my enemies by my hand, like water breaking through." That is why that place was named Baal-perazim.
en.R: So David and his men went up to Baal-perazim, and David defeated the Philistines there. He said, "God has used me to break through my enemies, the way a flood breaks through." That is why the place was called Baal-perazim, which means "Master of breaking through."

es.L: Y subieron a Baal-perazim, y allí los hirió David, y dijo David: «Dios ha abierto brecha entre mis enemigos por mi mano, como una brecha de aguas». Por eso llamaron el nombre de aquel lugar Baal-perazim.
es.B: Así que subieron a Baal-perazim, y allí David los derrotó. Dijo: «Dios ha irrumpido entre mis enemigos por mi mano, como el agua que rompe un dique». Por eso aquel lugar se llamó Baal-perazim.
es.R: Así que David y sus hombres subieron a Baal-perazim, y allí David derrotó a los filisteos. Dijo: «Dios se ha valido de mí para abrirse paso entre mis enemigos, como una inundación que lo arrasa todo». Por eso aquel lugar se llamó Baal-perazim, que significa «Señor de las brechas».

fr.L: Et ils montèrent à Baal-Peratsim, et David les frappa là, et David dit : « Dieu a fait une brèche dans mes ennemis par ma main, comme une brèche que font les eaux. » C’est pourquoi on appela ce lieu du nom de Baal-Peratsim.
fr.B: Ils montèrent donc à Baal-Peratsim, et David les battit là. Il dit : « Dieu a percé les rangs de mes ennemis par ma main, comme l’eau qui fait irruption. » C’est pourquoi on donna à ce lieu le nom de Baal-Peratsim.
fr.R: Alors David et ses hommes sont montés à Baal-Peratsim, et David a battu les Philistins. Il a dit : « Dieu s’est servi de moi pour enfoncer mes ennemis, comme une inondation qui emporte tout. » C’est pourquoi on a appelé cet endroit Baal-Peratsim, ce qui veut dire « Maître des percées ».

sw.L: Wakapanda Baal-perasimu, naye Daudi akawapiga huko, Daudi akasema, "Mungu amewavunja adui zangu kwa mkono wangu kama kuvunja kwa maji." Kwa hiyo wakaliita jina la mahali pale Baal-perasimu.
sw.B: Basi walipanda Baal-perasimu, naye Daudi akawashinda huko. Akasema, "Mungu amewavunja adui zangu kwa mkono wangu, kama maji yanavyobomoa kingo." Ndiyo sababu mahali pale paliitwa Baal-perasimu.
sw.R: Basi Daudi na watu wake walipanda Baal-perasimu, naye Daudi akawashinda Wafilisti huko. Akasema, "Mungu amenitumia kuvunja safu za adui zangu, kama mafuriko yanavyovunja kingo." Ndiyo sababu mahali pale paliitwa Baal-perasimu, maana yake "Bwana wa kuvunja."

vi.L: Họ đi lên Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim, và Đa-vít đánh bại chúng tại đó, và Đa-vít nói: "Đức Chúa Trời đã dùng tay tôi phá vỡ kẻ thù tôi như nước phá vỡ bờ." Vì thế người ta gọi tên nơi ấy là Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim.
vi.B: Vậy họ đi lên Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim, và Đa-vít đánh bại chúng tại đó. Ông nói: "Đức Chúa Trời đã dùng tay tôi phá tan kẻ thù như nước lũ vỡ bờ." Vì thế nơi ấy được gọi là Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít và người của ông đi lên Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim, và Đa-vít đánh bại người Phi-li-tin tại đó. Ông nói: "Đức Chúa Trời đã dùng tôi phá tan kẻ thù, như dòng nước lũ phá vỡ bờ đê." Vì thế nơi ấy được gọi là Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim, nghĩa là "Chủ Phá Vỡ".

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 바알브라심으로 올라갔고, 다윗이 거기에서 그들을 쳤다. 그리고 다윗이 말했다. "하나님께서 물이 터져 나가듯이 내 손으로 내 원수들을 터뜨리셨다." 그래서 그들이 그곳의 이름을 바알브라심이라고 불렀다.
ko.B: 그래서 그들은 바알브라심으로 올라갔고, 다윗은 거기에서 그들을 쳐부수었다. 그가 말했다. "하나님께서 물이 둑을 터뜨리듯 내 손으로 내 원수들을 터뜨려 무너뜨리셨다." 그래서 그곳을 바알브라심이라고 불렀다.
ko.R: 다윗과 그의 부하들은 바알브라심으로 올라갔고, 다윗은 거기에서 블레셋 사람들을 이겼다. 다윗이 말했다. "하나님께서 나를 쓰셔서, 홍수가 둑을 터뜨리듯이 내 원수들을 뚫고 나가셨다." 그래서 그곳을 '터뜨리시는 주인'이라는 뜻으로 바알브라심이라고 불렀다.

decisions.choice: like a breaking through of waters: like a flood bursting its banks
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:20: the picture is of water that breaks out suddenly and sweeps everything before it. God scattered the Philistines as swiftly as that.

decisions.choice: Baal-perazim: "master of breakings through"
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:20: Baal means "lord", "master" or "owner", and perazim comes from the verb "break through" in David's words. The name ties the place to what God did there. It is not certain whether "baal" here points to God as master, or whether the place already bore a name linked with the Canaanite god Baal and David's words give it a new meaning.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 5:20
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:20 says "David came"; Chronicles says "they went up", David and his army. Chronicles has "God" where 2 Samuel has "Yahweh", and "by my hand" where 2 Samuel has "before me": God broke through, using David as his means. Chronicles also says "they called" the place, where 2 Samuel has "he called".

decisions.choice: Perazim: recalled in Isaiah 28:21
decisions.reason: Isaiah warns that Yahweh will rise up "as at Mount Perazim", but this time against his own people. The same verb "break through" is used of Yahweh's anger against Uzzah in 13:11 (Perez-uzza).

decisions.choice: was named (Balanced, Readable); David and his men; God has used me to; which means "Master of breaking through" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the passive for "they called". Readable names who "they" are, turns "by my hand" into "used me", and explains the meaning of the name so that the reader sees the wordplay, as at 2 Samuel 5:20.

decisions.choice: Mungu ... kwa mkono wangu
decisions.reason: Chronicles has "God" and "by my hand" where 2 Samuel 5:20 has "Yahweh" and "before me"; the Swahili of Samuel changes only these words.

source.text: וַיַּעַזְבוּ־שָׁ֖ם אֶת־אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔יד וַיִּשָּׂרְפ֖וּ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And they abandoned there their gods, and said David, and they were burned with fire.

en.L: And they abandoned their gods there, and David gave command, and they were burned with fire.
en.B: The Philistines left their gods behind there, and at David's command they were burned up.
en.R: The Philistines ran away and left the images of their gods behind. David gave orders, and the images were burned.

es.L: Y abandonaron allí sus dioses, y David dio orden, y fueron quemados en el fuego.
es.B: Los filisteos dejaron allí sus dioses, y por orden de David fueron quemados.
es.R: Los filisteos huyeron y dejaron atrás las imágenes de sus dioses. David dio la orden, y las imágenes fueron quemadas.

fr.L: Et ils abandonnèrent là leurs dieux, et David donna un ordre, et ils furent brûlés au feu.
fr.B: Les Philistins laissèrent là leurs dieux, et sur l’ordre de David on les brûla.
fr.R: Les Philistins se sont enfuis en laissant derrière eux les statues de leurs dieux. David a donné un ordre, et on a brûlé ces statues.

sw.L: Wakaiacha miungu yao huko, naye Daudi akatoa amri, nayo ikachomwa kwa moto.
sw.B: Wafilisti waliiacha miungu yao huko, na kwa amri ya Daudi ikachomwa moto.
sw.R: Wafilisti walikimbia wakaziacha sanamu za miungu yao. Daudi akatoa amri, na sanamu hizo zikachomwa moto.

vi.L: Chúng bỏ lại các thần của chúng tại đó, và Đa-vít ra lệnh, và chúng bị đốt trong lửa.
vi.B: Người Phi-li-tin bỏ lại các thần của họ tại đó, và theo lệnh Đa-vít, các thần ấy bị đốt đi.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin bỏ chạy, để lại các tượng thần của họ. Đa-vít ra lệnh, và người ta đốt các tượng ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 거기에 자기들의 신들을 버렸다. 그리고 다윗이 명령하여 그것들이 불에 태워졌다.
ko.B: 블레셋 사람들은 자기들의 신들을 거기에 버리고 갔다. 다윗이 명령하자 그것들은 불에 태워졌다.
ko.R: 블레셋 사람들은 달아나면서 자기들의 신상들을 버리고 갔다. 다윗은 명령을 내려 그 신상들을 불태우게 했다.

decisions.choice: their gods: the images of their gods, brought to battle for protection
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:21, armies carried images of their gods into battle, as Israel once carried the ark (1 Samuel 4:3-11). Here the Philistines flee and leave their gods behind.

decisions.choice: burned with fire: where 2 Samuel 5:21 says David and his men carried them away
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:21 calls them "their idols" and says "David and his men carried them away". Chronicles calls them "their gods" and says that David gave orders and they were burned, as the law commanded for the images of the nations' gods (Deuteronomy 7:5, 25). The two accounts may describe two steps: the idols were taken, then destroyed.

decisions.choice: said: gave command
decisions.reason: The plain verb "say" is used here, as often, for a king giving an order.

decisions.choice: The Philistines (Balanced, Readable); ran away; the images of their gods (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Philistines as the subject. Readable adds "ran away", since leaving their gods behind shows that they fled, and says "images" so that the burning is clear.

decisions.choice: "신들" (L, B); "신상들" (R)
decisions.reason: Chronicles says "their gods" where 2 Samuel 5:21 has "their idols"; Literal and Balanced keep "gods", and Readable says "images of gods", as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: And added again Philistines and made a raid in the valley.

en.L: And [the] Philistines yet again made a raid in the valley.
en.B: Once again the Philistines made a raid on the valley.
en.R: Later the Philistines came back again and raided the valley.

es.L: Y volvieron otra vez los filisteos e hicieron una incursión en el valle.
es.B: Una vez más los filisteos hicieron una incursión en el valle.
es.R: Más tarde los filisteos volvieron y saquearon el valle.

fr.L: Et les Philistins firent encore une incursion dans la vallée.
fr.B: Une fois encore, les Philistins vinrent piller la vallée.
fr.R: Plus tard, les Philistins sont revenus faire un raid dans la vallée.

sw.B: Kwa mara nyingine Wafilisti walivamia bonde hilo.
sw.R: Baadaye Wafilisti walirudi tena wakavamia bonde hilo.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin lại cướp phá trong thung lũng lần nữa.
vi.B: Một lần nữa người Phi-li-tin cướp phá thung lũng.
vi.R: Sau đó người Phi-li-tin lại kéo đến cướp phá thung lũng.

ko.L: 그리고 블레셋 사람들이 다시 그 골짜기를 습격했다.
ko.B: 블레셋 사람들이 다시 그 골짜기를 습격했다.
ko.R: 나중에 블레셋 사람들이 또 와서 그 골짜기를 습격했다.

decisions.choice: added again: a second attack
decisions.reason: The verb "add" with another verb means to do something again, as at 2 Samuel 5:22.

decisions.choice: differences from 2 Samuel 5:22
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:22 says the Philistines "came up yet again and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim". Chronicles says they "made a raid" (as in verse 9) and calls the place simply "the valley", the one named in verse 9.

decisions.choice: Later ... came back
decisions.reason: Readable says "came back" so that the second raid is clearly a return, as at 2 Samuel 5:22.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל ע֤וֹד דָּוִיד֙ בֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֥א תַֽעֲלֶ֖ה אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם הָסֵב֙ מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וּבָ֥אתָ לָהֶ֖ם מִמּ֥וּל הַבְּכָאִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And inquired again David of God, and said to him God, Not you shall go up after them; turn away from them, and come to them from in front of the balsam trees.

en.L: And David inquired again of God, and God said to him, "You shall not go up after them; turn away from them, and come upon them in front of the balsam trees.
en.B: When David inquired of God again, God answered him, "Do not go up after them. Circle away from them and attack them opposite the balsam trees.
en.R: David asked God again what to do, and God answered, "Do not go straight after them. Go around them another way and attack them near the balsam trees.

es.L: Y consultó otra vez David a Dios, y Dios le dijo: «No subirás tras ellos; rodéalos, apartándote de ellos, y ven contra ellos frente a los árboles de bálsamo.
es.B: Cuando David volvió a consultar a Dios, Dios le respondió: «No subas tras ellos. Rodéalos apartándote de ellos y atácalos frente a los árboles de bálsamo.
es.R: David volvió a preguntarle a Dios qué debía hacer, y Dios le respondió: «No los persigas de frente. Rodéalos por otro camino y atácalos cerca de los árboles de bálsamo.

fr.L: Et David consulta encore Dieu, et Dieu lui dit : « Tu ne monteras pas derrière eux ; détourne-toi d’eux, et arrive sur eux en face des baumiers.
fr.B: Quand David consulta Dieu de nouveau, Dieu lui répondit : « Ne monte pas à leur poursuite. Écarte-toi d’eux et attaque-les du côté des baumiers.
fr.R: David a de nouveau demandé à Dieu ce qu’il devait faire, et Dieu a répondu : « Ne les poursuis pas directement. Fais un détour pour les contourner, et attaque-les près des baumiers.

sw.L: Daudi akamwuliza Mungu tena, naye Mungu akamwambia, "Usipande ukiwafuata; geuka uwaache, uwajie mbele ya miti ya balsamu.
sw.B: Daudi alipomwuliza Mungu tena, Mungu alimjibu, "Usipande ukiwafuata. Zunguka mbali nao, uwashambulie ukitokea upande wa miti ya balsamu.
sw.R: Daudi alimwuliza Mungu tena afanye nini, naye Mungu akamjibu, "Usiwafuate moja kwa moja. Zunguka kwa njia nyingine, uwashambulie karibu na miti ya balsamu.

vi.L: Đa-vít lại cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời, và Đức Chúa Trời phán với ông: "Ngươi chớ đi lên đuổi theo chúng; hãy đi vòng tránh chúng và đến đánh chúng ở phía trước những cây bóp-ca.
vi.B: Khi Đa-vít cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời lần nữa, Đức Chúa Trời đáp: "Đừng đi lên đuổi theo chúng. Hãy đi vòng tránh chúng và đánh chúng ở phía đối diện những cây bóp-ca.
vi.R: Đa-vít lại hỏi Đức Chúa Trời nên làm gì, và Đức Chúa Trời đáp: "Đừng đuổi thẳng theo chúng. Hãy đi vòng đường khác và tấn công chúng gần những cây bóp-ca.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 다시 하나님께 여쭈자, 하나님께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "그들을 따라 올라가지 마라. 그들에게서 돌아서서, 발삼나무 숲 맞은편에서 그들에게 가거라.
ko.B: 다윗이 다시 하나님께 여쭈자, 하나님께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "그들을 뒤쫓아 올라가지 마라. 그들을 피해 돌아가서 발삼나무 숲 맞은편에서 그들을 쳐라.
ko.R: 다윗이 다시 하나님께 어떻게 해야 할지 여쭈었다. 하나님께서 대답하셨다. "그들을 곧바로 뒤쫓지 마라. 다른 길로 돌아가서 발삼나무 숲 근처에서 그들을 쳐라.

decisions.choice: balsam trees: a kind of tree, not certainly known
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:23: the word appears only there, in verse 24 and here and in verse 15. It may name the balsam, a shrub that gives a gum, or another tree such as the mulberry or poplar.

decisions.choice: go up after them; turn away from them: compared with 2 Samuel 5:23
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:23 has "You shall not go up; go around to behind them". Chronicles says "You shall not go up after them; turn away from them". The plan is the same seen from the other side: David is not to follow the Philistines straight on, but to circle away and come at them by another way. Chronicles again says "God" where 2 Samuel has "Yahweh".

decisions.choice: a different plan from the first battle
decisions.reason: The first time God said "Go up" (verse 10); now he forbids a direct attack. Victory comes by asking again and obeying each new word, not by repeating what worked before.

decisions.choice: Circle away from them (Balanced); Do not go straight after them. Go around them another way (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that only a direct pursuit is forbidden; David is still to fight, coming at the enemy from another side.

source.text: וִ֠יהִי כְּֽשָׁמְעֲךָ֞ אֶת־ק֤וֹל הַצְּעָדָה֙ בְּרָאשֵׁ֣י הַבְּכָאִ֔ים אָ֖ז תֵּצֵ֣א בַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה כִּֽי־יָצָ֤א הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־מַחֲנֵ֥ה פְלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And let it be, when you hear the sound of the marching in [the] tops of the balsam trees, then you shall go out into the battle, for has gone out God before you to strike [the] camp of Philistines.

en.L: And let it be, when you hear the sound of the marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then you shall go out to battle, for God has gone out before you to strike the camp of [the] Philistines."
en.B: The moment you hear the sound of marching along the tops of the balsam trees, go out to battle, for God has gone out ahead of you to strike down the Philistine army."
en.R: As soon as you hear marching up in the tops of the balsam trees, go out and fight. God has gone ahead of you to defeat the Philistine army."

es.L: Y sucederá que, cuando oigas el ruido de marcha en las copas de los árboles de bálsamo, entonces saldrás a la batalla, porque Dios habrá salido delante de ti para herir el campamento de los filisteos».
es.B: En cuanto oigas el ruido de pasos por las copas de los árboles de bálsamo, sal a la batalla, porque Dios ha salido delante de ti para derrotar al ejército filisteo».
es.R: Tan pronto como oigas ruido de pasos en lo alto de los árboles de bálsamo, sal a pelear. Dios va delante de ti para derrotar al ejército filisteo».

fr.L: Et qu’il en soit ainsi : quand tu entendras le bruit d’une marche dans la cime des baumiers, alors tu sortiras au combat, car Dieu sera sorti devant toi pour frapper le camp des Philistins. »
fr.B: Dès que tu entendras un bruit de pas à la cime des baumiers, sors pour le combat, car Dieu est sorti devant toi pour battre l’armée des Philistins. »
fr.R: Dès que tu entendras un bruit de marche en haut des baumiers, sors et combats. Dieu sera parti devant toi pour battre l’armée des Philistins. »

sw.L: Na iwe, utakaposikia sauti ya kutembea juu ya vilele vya miti ya balsamu, ndipo utatoka vitani, kwa maana Mungu ametoka mbele yako kulipiga jeshi la Wafilisti."
sw.B: Mara utakaposikia sauti ya watu wanaotembea juu ya vilele vya miti ya balsamu, toka uende vitani, kwa maana Mungu ametoka akutangulie kulishinda jeshi la Wafilisti."
sw.R: Mara utakaposikia sauti ya kutembea juu kwenye vilele vya miti ya balsamu, toka ukapigane. Mungu amekutangulia kulishinda jeshi la Wafilisti."

vi.L: Khi nào ngươi nghe tiếng bước chân đi trên ngọn những cây bóp-ca, thì hãy ra trận, vì Đức Chúa Trời đã ra đi trước ngươi để đánh trại quân Phi-li-tin."
vi.B: Ngay khi con nghe tiếng bước quân đi trên ngọn những cây bóp-ca, hãy ra trận, vì Đức Chúa Trời đã ra đi trước con để đánh tan quân Phi-li-tin."
vi.R: Ngay khi con nghe tiếng bước quân trên ngọn những cây bóp-ca, hãy ra đánh. Đức Chúa Trời đã đi trước con để đánh bại quân Phi-li-tin."

ko.L: 그리고 발삼나무 꼭대기에서 행군하는 소리가 들리거든, 그때 너는 싸우러 나가거라. 하나님께서 블레셋 사람들의 진영을 치시려고 네 앞에 나가셨기 때문이다."
ko.B: 발삼나무 꼭대기에서 행군하는 소리가 들리면 곧바로 싸우러 나가거라. 하나님께서 블레셋 군대를 치시려고 너보다 앞서 나가셨다."
ko.R: 발삼나무 꼭대기에서 행군하는 소리가 들리면 바로 나가서 싸워라. 하나님께서 블레셋 군대를 무찌르시려고 너보다 먼저 나가셨다."

decisions.choice: the sound of marching in the treetops: the sign that God's own army is advancing
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:24: the marching is heard above the trees, where no soldiers walk. It is the sound of God going out to battle at the head of his heavenly army (Judges 4:14; 5:4). David is to follow where God has gone first.

decisions.choice: go out to battle: where 2 Samuel 5:24 says "act quickly"
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:24 says "then you shall act quickly, for then Yahweh has gone out". Chronicles says "then you shall go out to battle, for God has gone out". The words "go out" are now used both of David and of God: when God goes out, David goes out after him.

decisions.choice: the camp: the army in its camp
decisions.reason: The word means a camp and also the army that camps in it, as at 2 Samuel 5:24.

decisions.choice: the Philistine army
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "army", since it is the fighting force that is struck. Readable makes the last clause its own sentence.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ דָּוִ֔יד כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖הוּ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּכּוּ֙ אֶת־מַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מִגִּבְע֖וֹן וְעַד־גָּֽזְרָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And did David as had commanded him God, and they struck [the] camp of Philistines from Gibeon and to Gezer.

en.L: And David did as God had commanded him, and they struck the camp of [the] Philistines from Gibeon as far as Gezer.
en.B: David did exactly what God had commanded him, and they struck down the Philistine army all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.
en.R: David did what God had told him. He and his men defeated the Philistine army and chased them all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

es.L: E hizo David como Dios le había mandado, e hirieron el campamento de los filisteos desde Gabaón hasta Gezer.
es.B: David hizo exactamente lo que Dios le había mandado, y derrotaron al ejército filisteo desde Gabaón hasta Gezer.
es.R: David hizo lo que Dios le había dicho. Él y sus hombres derrotaron al ejército filisteo y lo persiguieron desde Gabaón hasta Gezer.

fr.L: Et David fit comme Dieu le lui avait commandé, et ils frappèrent le camp des Philistins depuis Gabaon jusqu’à Guézer.
fr.B: David fit exactement ce que Dieu lui avait commandé, et ils battirent l’armée des Philistins depuis Gabaon jusqu’à Guézer.

sw.L: Daudi akafanya kama Mungu alivyomwamuru, wakalipiga jeshi la Wafilisti kutoka Gibeoni mpaka Gezeri.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 하나님께서 그에게 명령하신 대로 했고, 그들이 기브온에서부터 게셀에 이르기까지 블레셋 사람들의 진영을 쳤다.
ko.B: 다윗은 하나님께서 명령하신 대로 그대로 했다. 그리고 그들은 기브온에서부터 게셀까지 블레셋 군대를 쳐부수었다.
ko.R: 다윗은 하나님께서 말씀하신 대로 했다. 다윗과 그의 부하들은 블레셋 군대를 쳐부수고, 기브온에서부터 게셀까지 그들을 쫓아갔다.

decisions.choice: Gibeon: where 2 Samuel 5:25 reads Geba
decisions.reason: Chronicles reads Gibeon, a town northwest of Jerusalem on the road down to the west, and Isaiah 28:21 also names the valley of Gibeon beside Mount Perazim. The Hebrew of 2 Samuel 5:25 reads Geba, a town north of Jerusalem in Benjamin. Gibeon fits the line of flight toward Gezer well.

decisions.choice: other differences from 2 Samuel 5:25
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:25 says "he struck the Philistines ... until you come to Gezer". Chronicles says "they struck the camp of the Philistines", David and his army together, and "to Gezer". It again has "God" where 2 Samuel has "Yahweh".

decisions.choice: David did as God had commanded: obedience, then victory
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:25, the story ends with David doing exactly what God said. Chronicles sets this against Saul, who died for his unfaithfulness and because he did not seek Yahweh (10:13-14); David asks and obeys.

decisions.choice: Gezer: at the edge of the coastal plain
decisions.reason: Gezer stood where the hills meet the plain. David drove the Philistines out of the hills and back toward their own land.

decisions.choice: He and his men; defeated ... and chased them
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are and splits the verb into "defeated" and "chased", since "struck ... from Gibeon to Gezer" describes a pursuit across the country, as at 2 Samuel 5:25.

records.literal_gloss: And went out [the] name of David into all the lands, and Yahweh put the dread of him on all the nations.

en.L: And the name of David went out into all the lands, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put the dread of him on all the nations.
en.B: So David's fame spread through every land, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made all the nations dread him.
en.R: David became famous in every country, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made all the nations afraid of him.

es.L: Y salió el nombre de David por todas las tierras, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} puso el temor de él sobre todas las naciones.
es.B: Así la fama de David se extendió por todas las tierras, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo que todas las naciones le tuvieran temor.
es.R: David llegó a ser famoso en todos los países, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo que todas las naciones le tuvieran miedo.

fr.L: Et le nom de David se répandit dans tous les pays, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mit la terreur de lui sur toutes les nations.
fr.B: La renommée de David se répandit donc dans tous les pays, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fit que toutes les nations le redoutèrent.
fr.R: David est devenu célèbre dans tous les pays, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait que toutes les nations avaient peur de lui.

sw.L: Jina la Daudi likaenea katika nchi zote, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaweka hofu yake juu ya mataifa yote.
sw.B: Basi sifa za Daudi zikaenea katika kila nchi, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akayafanya mataifa yote yamwogope.
sw.R: Daudi akajulikana katika kila nchi, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akayafanya mataifa yote yamwogope.

vi.B: Vậy danh tiếng Đa-vít lan khắp mọi xứ, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} khiến mọi dân tộc kinh sợ ông.
vi.R: Đa-vít trở nên nổi tiếng trong mọi xứ, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} khiến mọi dân tộc đều sợ ông.

ko.B: 그래서 다윗의 명성이 모든 나라에 퍼졌고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모든 민족이 그를 두려워하게 하셨다.
ko.R: 다윗은 모든 나라에 이름이 알려졌다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모든 민족이 다윗을 두려워하게 하셨다.

decisions.choice: a closing verse with no parallel in 2 Samuel
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5 ends with the victory of verse 25. Chronicles adds this summary of its own. Its words recall Yahweh's promise to Israel at the edge of the land: "I will begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you on the peoples" (Deuteronomy 2:25; 11:25). What was promised to the people is now given through their king.

decisions.choice: the name of David went out: his fame spread
decisions.reason: A "name" is a reputation. Yahweh promised David a great name (17:8), and here it begins to spread beyond Israel.

decisions.choice: the dread of him: dread of David
decisions.reason: "Him" is David. The nations fear David, but it is Yahweh who puts that fear on them.

decisions.choice: fame (Balanced); became famous (Readable); dread him / afraid of him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "fame" for "name" and turn "put the dread of him on" into a verb.
